# iCloud Calendar MCP

> An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI assistants read and change iCloud Calendar over CalDAV. It runs on the user's computer with Java 21 or newer, talks only to iCloud, and sends no telemetry. Free and open source under Apache-2.0. Made by OneKash Labs (https://onekash.org). Not affiliated with Apple.

Website: https://mcp.onekash.org
Source: https://github.com/icloud-calendar-mcp/icloud-calendar-mcp
Full reference: https://github.com/icloud-calendar-mcp/icloud-calendar-mcp#readme

## Never use the Apple ID password

The server signs in with an app-specific password (https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204397), which can be revoked at any time without affecting the Apple ID. The user name is the full iCloud email address.

## Set up

1. Install Java 21 or newer. Every install option runs the same Java build; npx and uvx download and launch the JAR but don't replace the JVM.
2. Create an app-specific password.
3. Add the server to the MCP client's configuration, then restart the client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "icloud-calendar": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@icloud-calendar-mcp/server"],
      "env": {
        "ICLOUD_USERNAME": "your-apple-id@icloud.com",
        "ICLOUD_PASSWORD": "your-app-specific-password"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

With Python, use `"command": "uvx", "args": ["icloud-calendar-mcp"]`. With the JAR, use `"command": "java", "args": ["-jar", "/path/to/icloud-calendar-mcp-all.jar"]`.

In Claude Desktop the configuration file is `claude_desktop_config.json`, in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/` on macOS, `~/.config/claude/` on Linux, and `%APPDATA%\Claude\` on Windows.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Changes the calendar |
|------|--------------|----------------------|
| `list_calendars` | Lists the account's calendars | No |
| `get_events` | Reads the events in a date range from one calendar | No |
| `create_event` | Adds an event: all-day or timed, repeating or not, with optional alarms | Adds |
| `update_event` | Changes only the fields passed; one occurrence, this and later, or the whole series | Changes |
| `delete_event` | Deletes one occurrence, this and later, or the whole series | Deletes |

Also: the `calendar://calendars` resource, and three prompts: `schedule_meeting`, `reschedule`, and `find_conflicts`.

Things to know:
- `get_events` and `create_event` return a `handle` for each event. Pass it to `update_event` or `delete_event`; it works across sessions and restarts. If the event changed elsewhere since the handle was issued, the edit reports a conflict instead of overwriting.
- A recurring series comes back as one result per occurrence. Editing or deleting an occurrence needs `scope`: `this_occurrence`, `this_and_future`, or `all_events`. Without it the request is rejected, so a single-occurrence edit never changes the whole series by accident.
- `get_events` selects whole UTC days. The range is capped at 366 days and the response at 1,000 events; a wider request returns a clear error instead of a cut-off list.
- iCloud can take a moment to list a just-created event.

## Why this server

- Runs anywhere a JVM runs: Windows, macOS, or Linux. It doesn't depend on macOS, AppleScript, or the Calendar app.
- Durable event handles across sessions.
- Correct recurrence: single occurrences, this and future, or the whole series.
- Bounded responses with clear errors.
- Published on the MCP Registry, npm, and PyPI.

## Security and privacy

- Talks only to the user's computer (over STDIO) and to iCloud (caldav.icloud.com). No telemetry.
- Credentials come from environment variables only and are never logged or shown in errors.
- 282 security tests, covering the OWASP MCP Top 10.
- Rate limits: 60 reads and 20 writes a minute.
- Blocks requests to internal addresses and dangerous URI schemes (SSRF protection).
- Adds, changes, and deletes are logged through the MCP logging protocol.
- Security policy: https://github.com/icloud-calendar-mcp/icloud-calendar-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
